_what_this_is: The working recipe behind scripts/demo/record-demo.mjs, which regenerates docs/demo.gif (the animated demo in README.md). To reshoot it: `npm run build` then `npm run demo:record`.
prereqs: npm run build  — dist/card.js must be current; the recorder loads that exact bundle, not src/
ffmpeg on PATH — two-pass palette GIF encode
npx playwright install chromium — once per machine; `playwright` is a devDependency
hard_constraints: The recorder only navigates and clicks real controls on its own standalone rig, scripts/demo/record-harness.html. It never writes to src/, dist/ (rebuild with `npm run build`), or any docs/ file other than the output gif.
scripts/demo/record-harness.html is committed so the recipe is reproducible without rebuilding the rig from scratch. It is NOT a user-facing page — there is no docs/index.html demo for this card.

sections: NBA — 6 rows (sensor.nba_, view schedule, special bos)
NHL — 6 rows (sensor.nhl_, view schedule, special col)
Premier League — 6 rows (sensor.epl_, view schedule, special liv)
card_setConfig.note: every section uses `view: schedule` (the default) — one row per game, live (IN) games first, then every other game by |date − now|. `slide_sec` is 4 and the recorder holds long on each slide so all six rows are readable.

harness_config.fake_data: Six games per tracked sensor (home side only, so each fixture is one row), a mix of IN / POST / PRE states with team names, records, scores, TV networks, real ESPN CDN logo URLs (https — non-https logos are dropped by the card) and a relative ISO `date` (minutes offset from Date.now()) so the by-date sort orders live games first then by nearness to now. NBA/NHL logos are keyed by team abbreviation; ESPN soccer logos are keyed by NUMERIC team id (see the EPL block). No real Home Assistant, no WebSocket: the harness gives the card a connection object with no subscribeEvents, so the card re-renders on every `card.hass = …` assignment (SubscriptionManager bails out early). The same connection object is reused across assignments so the card never treats it as a reconnect.
harness_config.mount_order: createElement → setConfig → appendChild → set .hass. setConfig before connecting matters for the same reason it does elsewhere in this card family.
harness_config.recorder_hook: window.__bumpScore() rewrites sensor.nba_bos with a higher score and re-assigns .hass, so the recorder can trigger the score-blink beat on camera.

recorder.capture_method: Real page.screenshot() with a fixed clip, sampled in a click / sleep / hold loop. Motion in the gif is the card's own CSS/JS (the slide swap, the post-goal score blink) sampled continuously — no synthetic cursor, no locator.click() teleport.
recorder.clip: measured once from #wrap's bounding box after window.__ready, reused for every frame; width/height rounded to even numbers for the encoder
recorder.encode: ffmpeg two-pass palette (palettegen max_colors=128 stats_mode=diff, paletteuse dither=bayer) scaled to 440px wide. Bump max_colors down if the gif is over ~1MB; the logos are the main colour cost.

scenario_beats: rest ~2s on the NBA section (6 rows — give the eye time)
click the ▸ (next section) button → NHL. rotation is already paused (prefers-reduced-motion). hold ~2.4s
click ▸ → wraps back to NBA. hold ~1.6s
call window.__bumpScore() — nba_bos ticks up while NBA is visible, so the score cell blinks on camera. hold ~2.8s
click the ▮▮/▶ toggle to start auto-advance; let it run ~5.6s (~1 swap at slide_sec 4). hold
hold ~1.2s of resting frames before the gif loops
known_risks: ESPN logo URLs (a.espncdn.com) can change their path scheme or rate-limit. If logos render blank, refresh the URLs in record-harness.html (the `L()` helper) against a current espn.com scoreboard, or inline a few as data: URIs. The recorder waits 2.5s after load for them; raise that if a re-shoot catches half-loaded logos. Some EPL numeric team ids in the new rows (Everton 368, Fulham 370, West Ham 371, Brentford 337) are best-effort — a wrong id just drops that one crest.
The demo config pins `layout.height` (268px) for 6 rows + header so every re-shoot records the same box. If you add rows or bump `layout.row_gap`, raise that height or the last row clips.

HACS renders a repo's README from its latest release tag, not from main. Merging a demo.gif change to main does not update what HACS users see until a new version is tagged. The README badge points at raw.githubusercontent.com/…/main/…, which is not tag-pinned and updates on every push.
